correctness.rationale: A generic diagonal row-column one-parameter subgroup has pairwise distinct weights on all matrix coordinates, and matrix Schubert varieties are invariant under this action. Thus the projective fixed points are coordinate matrices. For E_ij, northwest ranks are zero until both cutoffs include (i,j), then one; monotonicity reduces membership to r_w(i,j)>=1. This is equivalent to i>=m_j and gives the exact fixed-point count. The sharp bounds and equality cases are direct consequences of permutation prefix minima. The packaged checker exhaustively replays coordinate membership for every permutation through n=7.

value.rationale: Matrix Schubert varieties are central in Schubert calculus, determinantal geometry, Gröbner theory, and Grothendieck-polynomial geometry. The theorem gives a closed topological invariant for every permutation, shows that it depends only on left-to-right minima despite much richer geometry, and sharply classifies both extrema. The maximum criterion exhibits large families of proper nonlinear matrix Schubert varieties with the same Euler characteristic as ambient projective space. This is an all-family structural collapse of a natural invariant, not a finite parameter slice.
